name: Daya Bay Reactor Neutrino Experiment

intervals.label: six-AD configuration (includes the 2012 discovery)
intervals.quote: From 24 December 2011 to 28 July 2012 (217 days), the experiment ran in an initial six-AD configuration
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: replaces the earlier null-dated interval (sourced only to a 55-day exposure figure in the 2012 discovery paper's abstract, with no calendar dates) with day-precision dates from the Daya Bay Collaboration's own final-result paper.

intervals.label: eight-AD full configuration operation
intervals.quote: this eight-AD configuration was operated from 19 October 2012 until 20 December 2016 (1524 days)
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: replaces the earlier approximate '2012'-'2020' interval (sourced to Wikipedia and a detector-assembly paper abstract, with no exact dates) with day-precision dates from the Daya Bay Collaboration's own final-result paper. The prior interval conflated the eight-AD and seven-AD configurations into one row; they are now split (next interval).

intervals.label: seven-AD configuration (one AD re-purposed for JUNO-related R&D)
intervals.quote: Seven-AD operation occurred from 26 January 2017 until 12 December 2020 (1417 days) with one AD in EH1 re-purposed for liquid scintillator R&D for the JUNO experiment
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: new interval, split out from the prior single '8-AD' row. Final day of data taking (12 December 2020) is the source for the 'completed' interval below.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.quote: Seven-AD operation occurred from 26 January 2017 until 12 December 2020 (1417 days)
intervals.note: CORRECTED 2026-09-18: prior value ('2020', confidence approximate) was sourced only to Wikipedia; now day-precision and verified directly against the Daya Bay Collaboration's own final-result paper, which confirms the last day of data taking was 12 December 2020.

physics_goals.value: Measure the neutrino mixing angle theta_13 using reactor antineutrino disappearance
physics_goals.quote: Observation of electron-antineutrino disappearance at Daya Bay

unique_capabilities.value: Multiple functionally identical antineutrino detectors deployed across near and far underground halls to cancel reactor-flux and detector systematics between near and far measurements

quantity.quote: flux-weighted baselines of 470 m and 576 m
quantity.note: Two near halls (Daya Bay near and Ling Ao near); the shorter of the two flux-weighted baselines is recorded as `value` and both are given in `display`.

summary.plain: An experiment in southern China that used clusters of detectors near and far from nuclear reactors to discover that one type of neutrino oscillation, long searched for, really happens.
summary.technical: Reactor-antineutrino oscillation experiment using up to eight functionally identical Gd-doped liquid-scintillator antineutrino detectors at near (470 m, 576 m) and far (1648 m) underground halls from six 2.9 GW_th reactor cores at the Daya Bay/Ling Ao nuclear power complex, Guangdong, China. Its 2012 result was the first observation of a non-zero theta_13 mixing angle via reactor antineutrino disappearance.
